title: Less is More: Efficient Black-box Attribution via Minimal Interpretable Subset Selection
abstract: arXiv:2504.00470v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: To develop a trustworthy AI system, it is essential to understand its behavior using attribution methods, which aim to identify the input regions that most influence the model's decisions. For discrete inputs such as images, however, accurately identifying input-prediction interactions is particularly challenging because of combinatorial explosion. We formulate black-box attribution as an ordered interpretable subset-selection problem. Inspired by the marginal-gain principle of submodular optimization, the formulation permits redundancy, positive complementarity, and negative interference among input sub-regions. We propose LiMA (Less input is More faithful for Attribution), which ranks sub-regions by their contributions along a sequence of selected subsets. translated_title: 少即是多：通过最小可解释子集选择实现高效黑盒归因
translated_abstract: 为了构建可信赖的AI系统，使用归因方法理解模型行为至关重要，归因方法旨在识别对模型决策影响最大的输入区域。然而，对于图像等离散输入，由于组合爆炸问题，准确识别输入与预测之间的交互尤其具有挑战性。我们将黑盒归因问题形式化为一个有序的可解释子集选择问题。受次模优化边际增益原理的启发，该形式化方法允许输入子区域之间存在冗余、正互补性和负干扰。我们提出了LiMA（Less input is More faithful for Attribution，即更少输入带来更忠实的归因），该方法通过一系列选定子集对子区域的贡献进行排序。LiMA采用一种复合目标函数，通过语义一致性、协作性、预测置信度和语义有效性来评估子集。我们进一步设计了一个双向……（原文摘要在此截断）
tldr: 提出LiMA方法，将黑盒归因形式化为有序可解释子集选择问题，借助次模优化的边际增益原理和综合评估语义一致性、协作性、预测置信度与语义有效性的复合目标，高效识别对模型决策最关键的输入区域。
en_tdlr: Proposes LiMA, which formulates black-box attribution as an ordered interpretable subset-selection problem, leveraging the marginal-gain principle of submodular optimization and a composite objective (semantic consistency, collaboration, prediction confidence, and semantic effectiveness) to efficiently identify the most influential input regions.
